program: Child-health policy, community engagement and youth mental-health implementation

what: The Children's Partnership advances California child health through policy advocacy, research and community partnerships.
Its work includes Medi-Cal renewal reform and a publicly financed high-school peer-support pilot.
The numerical scenario prices a possible renewal-policy benefit using all recipient costs; it does not measure the value of the full portfolio.
strengths: A concrete policy mechanism could reduce paperwork-related coverage gaps rather than merely generate advocacy outputs.
Current original accounts and a detailed pilot evaluation make the organization and implementation constraints inspectable.
Coalition, public-funding and clinical-transfer assumptions are separated and can be revised independently.
reservations: AB2201 was held in committee on August 13, 2026; future revival, appropriation and extra influence are subjective priors, not an observed opportunity with a calibrated probability.
The peer pilot lacks consistent baseline or controlled health outcomes; positive feedback cannot be converted to durable clinical gains.
The priced renewal slice excludes other portfolio benefits and harms, so its high conditional price must not be read as a complete ranking of TCP.

sections.what: TCP works on health coverage, youth mental health, immigrant-family safety, early care and education. Its [current budget assessment](https://childrenspartnership.org/news/state-builds-california-budget-for-child-health-equity/) describes both funded priorities and failures to fund its renewal and community-health-worker proposals. The ordinary [donation route](https://childrenspartnership.org/donate) supports this recipient, not an exclusively purchased renewal or counseling service.
sections.monitoring: The [year-one peer evaluation](https://childrenspartnership.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Peer_to_Peer_Y1_Impact_Report_Long_FINAL.pdf) reports 936 students using support at least once and 140 peer leaders; these groups are not added because overlap is unreported. Its methods note missing baseline data and inconsistent outcome tracking. A reported 96% feeling better immediately is not a controlled clinical effect. Funding-access delays limited implementation; final policy recommendations are scheduled for fall 2027. A [different peer-leader randomized trial](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12310-025-09802-w) found no overall attempt reduction and possible harm with poor implementation in younger students; it is a caution about fidelity, not an estimate of TCP's program.
sections.qualitative:
The strongest scalable mechanism reviewed is simpler income and asset verification at Medi-Cal renewal. TCP is one of six listed [AB2201 co-sponsors](https://childrenspartnership.org/news/medi-cal-renewal-relief-act-ab-2201-brings-back-proven-public-health-strategy/), not the sole producer of a policy change. The [official text](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260AB2201) requires an appropriation; the [history](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billHistoryClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260AB2201) shows it held on August 13. The scenario therefore concerns a future equivalent reform and its implementation, not credit for an enacted 2026 bill. Coverage can improve health and financial protection, but no monetary welfare benefit is relabeled as a QALY.

Net resources require genuine avoided expenditure or retained earnings after taxes, withdrawn benefits, commuting, opportunity costs and administration. Papertime may improve even without changed clinical coverage; medical cash protection depends on sustained counterfactual uninsurance. Positive overlap reduces gains only, and full negative costs remain across all reached households. Co-sponsor and geographic estimates must not be summed without joint overlap accounting.
sections.cost:
Conditional signed reference: about $160.13 million per ten equivalent healthy years, combining unchanged 0.928869 California clinical QALYs with 0.003483 household-resource equivalents at three years of full recipient spending ($14,929,704). Income equivalents are welfare comparisons, not clinical QALYs. The original health-only reference about $160.7 million and all original worlds remain diagnostics.

The conditional renewal-policy slice is about $160.7 million per 10 California QALYs. It charges three years of all-recipient spending ($14,929,704) and yields 0.929 discounted QALYs under explicit subjective policy and funding assumptions. This is not TCP's whole-portfolio health return. The [LAO's March forecast](https://lao.ca.gov/Publications/Report/5146) of 400,000 fewer enrollees by June 2028 from six-month renewals is only a scale anchor, not a forecast of AB2201's effect. We assume 10% is remediable, half avoids actual uninsurance, 0.02 QALY per insured year, two benefit years, 5% incremental coalition success, 10% TCP attribution and 25% gift additionality. The [Oregon experiment mapping](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8081392/) informs but does not establish the 0.02 transfer. Zero and negative net effects remain possible; favorable stress assumptions are not a confidence interval.

The current renewal account describes less paperwork, automatic renewals and re-enrollment burdens; the July budget says the renewal act received no funding. The model remains a future equivalent reform, with existing county automation, federal compliance and other advocates in the counterfactual. Already-funded premium delays, childcare slots or CHW training are not new donor wins. [Renewal mechanism](https://childrenspartnership.org/news/medi-cal-renewal-relief-act-ab-2201-brings-back-proven-public-health-strategy/) [Budget assessment](https://childrenspartnership.org/news/state-builds-california-budget-for-child-health-equity/)

The resource cohort includes all remediable renewal enrollees before the 50% clinical uninsurance adjustment: 400,000 forecast enrollees times10%remediable times5%incremental coalition implementation times10%TCP attribution times25%funding response gives50expected enrollee slots. Divide by a hypothetical two enrollees per household to obtain25joint household equivalents. These are weak distribution/adoption priors, not observed unique families; the LAO number is a forecast scale anchor, not an AB2201 effect. No probability or funding multiplier is applied twice.

Assume$10genuine annual paperwork/time savings per household, discount positive value50%for overlap with health/security, and subtract the full$2implementation/administration/time burden. At a hypothetical$20,000resource baseline, both joint groups centrally gain$3. Count two benefit years at years2and3, exactly the clinical timing, using0.5times group households times discounted years times log(1+net/baseline). Administrative resources are independent of clinical response. No retail care, insurer reimbursement or ordinary survivor earnings are household cash. All dollar/grouping coefficients are judgments, not measured gains.

A medical-spending sensitivity assigns$100actual avoided cash cost only to25%of the50%whose uninsurance is avoided; retain80%after taxes/benefit withdrawals and50%positive overlap before subtracting full burdens. Remaining households get only their joint administrative net change. Clinical-null financial-only, null/unknown resources, no-capacity/no-implementation and adverse burdens remain explicit. Disjoint public payer consumption and real-resource expense are alternative scopes for the same transfer, not additive duplicates. Childcare, CHW training, immigrant-family support and peer/youth programs may affect resources; missing causal reach and retained net earnings leave those pathways unknown.
sections.funding:
The [2025 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/464106389/202631969349302653/full) reports $4,976,568 expenses, $5,492,357 revenue and $3,239,977 unrestricted net assets; restricted net assets were $6,745,074. Functional spending was $4,034,623 program, $659,310 administration and $282,635 fundraising. [Schedule D](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202631969349302653/IRS990ScheduleD) reconciles audited expenses to the return and separately records $2 million agency funds. The [2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/464106389/202513179349310611/full) supplies the earlier comparative years. The pilot's [$8 million public award](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/newsroom-office-of-communications/california-launches-pilot-program-in-high-schools-to-support-youth-mental-health/) is not an ordinary-gift funding gap. Recognized recipient expenses are not all governmental implementation costs, and reserves do not establish that donations are unnecessary.

A targeted review of the original 2023–25 returns confirms no separately netted fundraising or inventory costs and no Schedule D donated-service expense adjustment. The 2023 and 2024 return totals already include $44,279 and $22,318 of speaking-event expenses excluded from the corresponding audited-statement presentation. Those amounts are not added twice. The 2025 reconciliation matches $4,976,568 without adjustment. These costs cover the recipient, not all public implementation resources.

model.costScope: All recipient accrual spending for three prospective years at FY2025 scale; no special gift restriction. Agency/public implementation spending is not added to recognized recipient expense. This is a private-donor price, not societal cost-effectiveness.
model.geographicAttribution: The modeled renewal population consists of California Medi-Cal residents; g=1 for this branch only. National policy spillovers, other TCP work and non-health welfare are excluded, not assumed geographically identical.
model.formula: C=3*E. A=1/(1+d)^2+1/(1+d)^3. Y=N*r*u*A*p*a*b. Q_CA=Y*q+Q_other. P10=10*C/Q_CA when Q_CA>0. Central Q_other=0 is an accounting exclusion for the priced slice, not a finding of no other benefit. Resource households=(C/(3E))*N*r*p*a*b/householdMembers BEFORE clinicalu; cashbenefit groups restricted to u*saverShare, paperwork effect/fullcosts all households. Joint net=positive-overlap-adjusted actual savings minus FULLburden; income=.5*sum(groupPeople*PVyears2and3*log1p(net/before)). Three-yearcost/horizon preserved; gift100000scalesboth.
model.counterfactual: Already planned county automation, federal compliance, other advocates and the funded pilot proceed without the additional ordinary gift. A future renewal reform must improve on that baseline; present AB2201 is held, not enacted. No effect from merely preserving current grant-supported activity is credited.
model.attribution: p is coalition-induced incremental implementation probability over a three-year support window, including revival/appropriation, not the chance some law passes. a assigns only TCP's portion of that coalition contribution. b discounts additional ordinary funding for substitution, reserves and marginal capacity. No six-way equal attribution inferred from co-sponsorship.
model.uncertainty: High structural and subjective uncertainty. This finite central is a policy-option planning prior, not an empirically identified posterior or total portfolio return. Other policy and pilot outcomes could dominate either way. Scenarios are stress cases, not bounds or confidence intervals. The utility prior represents expected net health area over the stated finite horizon, including treatment burden, within-horizon fade and competing mortality; it is not an endpoint score held indefinitely. No survival extension is credited. Household grouping, genuine paperwork/time saving, costs, baseline and medical cash incidence are judgments. Full childcare/CHW/workforce/peer and immigrant-family portfolio effects remain unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Discounted additional California person-years insured rather than uninsured due to a funding-sensitive renewal reform. Central 46.4434392122 additional insured person-years, converted to 0.9288687842 QALYs. Counts of bill supporters, school users, grants and favorable responses are not health outcomes.

inputs.name: u

inputs.name: q
